nodes.title: Outfitter
nodes.summary: Shared organization context for Outfitter.
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Organization context for Outfitter projects, people, technologies and agents.

## For agents

Link relevant projects and business units to this organization. Record verified context and distinguish proposed work from completed outcomes. This page does not grant permissions.

nodes.title: Unsupervised
nodes.summary: Shared organization context for Unsupervised.
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Organization context for Unsupervised projects, people, technologies and agents.

## For agents

Link relevant projects and business units to this organization. Do not infer ownership, employment or relationships from a name alone. This page does not grant permissions.

nodes.title: Merged pull requests
nodes.body:
Count distinct pull requests merged for the project during the reporting period. Count by repository and PR number, using merge time rather than creation or approval time.

- Unit: merged pull requests
- Target: not specified
- Source: repository merge records
- Repository scope and reporting period: to be configured

No observed value has been recorded.

nodes.title: Active users with a connection
nodes.body:
Count distinct active Outfitter users who have at least one connected Google Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack or GitHub account. Count each user once, regardless of how many qualifying connections they have.

- Unit: users
- Qualifying connections: Google Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, GitHub
- Target: not specified
- Activity definition and reporting window: to be specified before automated reporting
- Source: user activity and connector connection records

## Observations

This is a measurement definition; no current value has been recorded.

nodes.title: Stripe
nodes.summary: Organization behind Stripe payment services.
nodes.body:
## Stripe

Organization context for the Stripe payment technology. Link the service separately from its provider.

nodes.title: Stripe Payments
nodes.summary: Payment service and potential source of payment and revenue records.
nodes.body:
## Stripe Payments

A payment service. Projects can document intended use with `uses`; metric definitions can identify it as a proposed source through `measured_by`.

A graph relationship does not configure a Stripe connector, establish accounting treatment or prove that payments have been collected.

nodes.title: Google
nodes.summary: Organization behind Gmail and Google Calendar.
nodes.body:
## Google

Organization context for Gmail and Google Calendar. Product relationships are documented separately from Outfitter’s proposed use of those products.

nodes.title: Gmail
nodes.summary: Email technology linked to Outfitter’s communication context.
nodes.body:
## Gmail

Google email product. Outfitter’s proposed uses relationship documents email context and connector intent; it does not establish an active account connection.

nodes.title: Google Calendar
nodes.summary: Calendar technology linked to Outfitter’s scheduling context.
nodes.body:
## Google Calendar

Google calendar product. Its integration relationship with Gmail records scheduling and email interoperability context, separately from the Google provider relationship. Outfitter account access must be configured independently.

nodes.title: WhatsApp
nodes.summary: Messaging technology for Outfitter’s proposed communication context.
nodes.body:
## WhatsApp

Messaging product documented as a proposed Outfitter dependency. No connected account, installed connector or message access is implied.

nodes.title: iMessage
nodes.summary: Messaging technology for Outfitter’s communication context.
nodes.body:
## iMessage

Messaging product documented as an Outfitter dependency. Availability and account access depend on separately configured connectors; this page does not establish operational access.

nodes.title: Linq
nodes.summary: Provider of a messaging API with iMessage support.
nodes.body:
## Linq

Linq provides messaging APIs, including iMessage support, according to its [website](https://linqapp.com). Keep the provider separate from the Linq Messaging API technology and from iMessage itself.

nodes.title: Linq Messaging API
nodes.summary: Messaging API offering iMessage access; a proposed integration option for Outfitter.
nodes.body:
## Messaging API

Linq advertises API access to iMessage, RCS and SMS on its [website](https://linqapp.com). See the [API documentation](https://docs.linqapp.com).

## Outfitter context

Proposed provider for Outfitter’s iMessage connector. Outfitter uses Linq Messaging API, which integrates with iMessage. This records an integration option, not an installed connector, configured account or verified message delivery.

nodes.title: Codeberg e.V.
nodes.summary: Nonprofit umbrella organization backing Forgejo development.
nodes.body:
## Codeberg e.V.

Codeberg e.V. backs Forgejo development as its umbrella organization. Forgejo is developed by an independent community under that umbrella.

Source: [Codeberg documentation](https://docs.codeberg.org/getting-started/what-is-codeberg/).

nodes.title: Forgejo
nodes.summary: Community-developed software forge under the umbrella of Codeberg e.V.
nodes.body:
## Forgejo

A self-hosted software forge developed by a community under the umbrella of Codeberg e.V. The developed_by relationship records that organizational context, rather than asserting that Codeberg is the sole author.

Source: [Forgejo](https://forgejo.org/).

nodes.title: Approve Release
nodes.summary: Decide whether a release is approved.
nodes.body:
## Approve Release

The decision to approve a release for an organization. This type is distinct from publishing or executing the release. A concrete approval and its supporting evidence must be recorded by the relevant workflow.

nodes.title: Release approval authority
nodes.summary: Authority to decide whether a release is approved.
nodes.body:
## Authority

Permits the Approve Release decision type. The holder acts within the organization named by their role assignment. This does not bypass deployment permissions or existing release controls.

nodes.title: CTO release approval grant
nodes.summary: Grants the CTO role release-approval decision authority.
nodes.body:
## Grant

The CTO role receives Release approval authority. Holders inherit this documented authority only within the scope of their own role assignment. No individual release has been approved by creating this grant.

nodes.title: Data sovereignty
nodes.summary: Control where data is stored and processed, who can access it, and which infrastructure operates it.
nodes.body:
## Customer problem

Self-hosters and enterprises need control over where their data is stored and processed, who can access it, and the infrastructure used to operate their systems.

Outfitter aims to address this shared problem. Specific hosting, access-control and data-handling requirements must be recorded for each deployment; this problem page is not a claim that a deployment already meets them.

nodes.title: Self-hosters
nodes.summary: People and teams running software on infrastructure they control.
nodes.body:
## Customer context

An Outfitter customer segment that values control of its own infrastructure and data. Shares the Data sovereignty problem with enterprise customers.

nodes.title: Enterprise
nodes.summary: Organizations needing control over their data and deployment environment.
nodes.body:
## Customer context

An Outfitter customer segment with organizational requirements for data location, processing, access and infrastructure control. Shares the Data sovereignty problem with self-hosters.

nodes.title: Outfitter inference service
nodes.summary: Model inference service offered by Outfitter.
nodes.body:
## Service

Inference used to run model requests. Its offering defines customer pricing separately from the product; no provider tariff or model price is asserted here.

nodes.title: Outfitter resident agent service
nodes.summary: Resident agents performing assigned organizational roles.
nodes.body:
## Service

Resident agents operating in assigned roles. Commercial rates are attached to the offering’s role tiers. A purchased tier does not itself assign a role or grant authority.

nodes.title: Inference with markup
nodes.summary: Inference priced as provider cost plus an Outfitter markup.
nodes.body:
## Pricing basis

Customer inference price is provider inference cost plus Outfitter’s markup. The markup percentage, providers, models, currency and billing unit are not specified yet.

properties.pricing_notes: Provider cost plus markup. Markup percentage, currency and billing unit remain unspecified.

nodes.title: Role-priced resident agents
nodes.summary: Resident-agent pricing depends on the agent’s role.
nodes.body:
## Pricing basis

Resident-agent rates vary by role. Role tiers reference the same Role entities used for assignments; the price for each role and its billing interval remain unspecified.

Inference treatment within these tiers has not been defined. This offering does not configure billing or create resident runtimes.

properties.pricing_notes: Prices and billing intervals for each role remain unspecified.

nodes.title: 10K monthly inference revenue
nodes.summary: Reach 10,000 in inference revenue per month.
nodes.body:
## Target

Reach 10,000 in inference revenue per month.

## Progress

See the linked metric definition for counting rules. No measured progress has been recorded.

nodes.title: Monthly inference revenue
nodes.body:
Sum inference revenue for one calendar month.

- Target: 10,000 per month
- Currency: not specified; use one configured currency and do not combine currencies without a defined conversion method
- Scope: inference revenue; resident-agent subscription fees are separate
- Source: inference billing and revenue records
- Accounting basis, refunds, tax treatment, timezone and whether the target covers total inference charges or markup revenue: to be defined

No measured value or billing integration has been recorded.

nodes.title: 10 resident agents completing a workflow daily
nodes.summary: Each day, at least 10 distinct resident agents complete at least one workflow.
nodes.body:
## Target

Each day, at least 10 distinct resident agents complete at least one workflow.

## Progress

See the linked metric definition for counting rules. No measured progress has been recorded.

nodes.title: Daily resident agents with a completed workflow
nodes.body:
Count distinct resident-agent IDs with at least one successfully completed workflow during the reporting day.

- Target: 10 agents per day
- Unit: distinct resident agents
- An agent completing several workflows counts once that day
- Queued, running, failed or cancelled workflows do not count
- Source: resident-agent identity and workflow completion records
- Reporting timezone and production/test exclusions: to be configured

No measured value or automated counter has been recorded.

nodes.title: 10 reported self-hosted installations
nodes.summary: Reach 10 distinct self-hosted installations reported to Outfitter.
nodes.body:
## Target

Reach 10 distinct self-hosted installations reported to Outfitter.

## Progress

See the linked metric definition for counting rules. No measured progress has been recorded.

nodes.title: Reported self-hosted installations
nodes.body:
Count distinct self-hosted installations that report their installation to Outfitter.

- Target: 10 installations
- Unit: unique installation IDs, deduplicated across repeated reports
- Scope: self-hosted installations, excluding hosted Outfitter instances
- Source: voluntarily submitted installation reports
- Reporting period, test-instance exclusions and retirement handling: to be specified
- Do not estimate unreported installs or treat this definition as consent to collect telemetry

No measured value or reporting integration has been recorded.

nodes.title: Set Organization Goals
nodes.summary: Set an organization’s goals and measures of success.
nodes.body:
## Set Organization Goals

Choose or revise the organization’s goals and success measures. Record the actual decision separately, including the deciding person, scoped role assignment, rationale and goals established.

nodes.title: Organization goal-setting authority
nodes.summary: Authority to set goals within the role assignment’s organization.
nodes.body:
## Authority

Permits Set Organization Goals within the organization named by the holder’s RoleAssignment. It documents decision authority, not platform access or automatic goal execution.

nodes.title: CEO organization goal-setting grant
nodes.summary: Grants the CEO role organization goal-setting authority.
nodes.body:
## Grant

The CEO role may set goals within its assigned organization. Read the holder and scope from the RoleAssignment.
